## Purpose and deliverables
Surge XT is a C++ hybrid software synthesizer. CMake builds multiple host-facing products: Surge XT instrument plugins/standalone, a separate Surge FX processor, a command-line target, a headless test runner, and optional Python bindings. Main build orchestration is in `CMakeLists.txt`, `src/CMakeLists.txt`, and `resources/CMakeLists.txt`.

## Runtime entry points and host boundary
JUCE-based processor/editor pairs form the principal interactive entry points. The instrument wrapper is `src/surge-xt/SurgeSynthProcessor.cpp` with `src/surge-xt/SurgeSynthEditor.cpp`; the dedicated effect product uses `src/surge-fx/SurgeFXProcessor.cpp` and `src/surge-fx/SurgeFXEditor.cpp`. These adapt DAW/standalone lifecycle, audio/MIDI buffers, parameter automation, and UI calls to the shared engine. A CLI entry point also exists at `src/surge-xt/cli/cli-main.cpp`.

## Core synth engine and voice flow
`src/common/SurgeSynthesizer.cpp` is the central synth engine, with persistent resources/state supplied by `src/common/SurgeStorage.cpp` and patch representation in `src/common/SurgePatch.cpp`. Host MIDI/note events enter the engine, allocate/manage per-note voices, render audio blocks, then return stereo audio through the product processors. Per-voice synthesis is concentrated in `src/common/dsp/SurgeVoice.cpp`; voice state is separated in `src/common/dsp/SurgeVoiceState.h`. This engine layer is the key boundary between host wrappers/UI and real-time DSP.

## Sound generation, filtering, and modulation
Oscillator implementations are pluggable behind shared oscillator interfaces: `src/common/dsp/Oscillator.h`, `src/common/dsp/oscillators/WavetableOscillator.cpp`, and `src/common/dsp/oscillators/ModernOscillator.cpp` represent the synthesis family. Voice audio is shaped through filter-chain processing in `src/common/dsp/QuadFilterChain.cpp` and filter implementations such as `src/common/dsp/filters/VectorizedSVFilter.cpp`.

Modulation sources feed parameterized synthesis and effects. Core parameter/modulation definitions are in `src/common/Parameter.cpp` and `src/common/ModulationSource.cpp`; key source types include `src/common/dsp/modulators/LFOModulationSource.cpp`, `src/common/dsp/modulators/ADSRModulationSource.h`, and Lua-backed formula helpers in `src/common/dsp/modulators/FormulaModulationHelper.cpp`.

## Effects and external DSP integration
Effects are a distinct post-synthesis processing stage, organized around `src/common/dsp/Effect.cpp` and concrete processors under `src/common/dsp/effects/`, e.g. `DelayEffect.cpp`, `ConvolutionEffect.cpp`, and `NimbusEffect.cpp`. Airwindows effects are wrapped rather than exposed directly through `src/common/dsp/effects/airwindows/AirWindowsEffect.cpp`, backed by vendored sources in `libs/airwindows/src/`. The repository also includes SST DSP libraries, PFFFT, r8brain, and SIMD support under `libs/`, making third-party DSP code a material implementation boundary.

## Persistence, content, and extensibility
Patch discovery/querying is handled by `src/common/PatchDB.cpp` and `src/common/PatchDBQueryParser.cpp`; factory and third-party patches, FX presets, wavetables, modulation presets, skins, tuning definitions, and impulse responses are staged from `resources/data/`. Wavetable loading/generation is represented by `src/common/dsp/Wavetable.cpp` and `src/common/dsp/WtGenService.cpp`, including Lua scripting through `src/common/dsp/WavetableScriptEvaluator.cpp` and `src/lua/`.

UI skin data is modeled in `src/common/SkinModel.cpp` and applied by the JUCE GUI layer in `src/surge-xt/gui/SkinSupport.cpp`. Tuning integrates MTS-ESP via `src/common/MTSESPTuning.cpp` and vendored `libs/oddsound-mts/`.

## Control integrations and infrastructure
Open Sound Control is implemented separately for instrument and FX products in `src/surge-xt/osc/OpenSoundControl.cpp` and `src/surge-fx/FXOpenSoundControl.cpp`. Optional native Python access is built with pybind11 from `src/surge-python/surgepy.cpp`. Runtime dependencies include JUCE, LuaJIT, SQLite, and bundled content; there is no required network service at runtime.

CI spans GitHub Actions and Azure Pipelines (`.github/workflows/build-pr.yml`, `azure-pipelines.yml`). Cross-platform packaging targets Linux, macOS, and Windows installers; CMake supports Windows, macOS, Linux, ARM/aarch64 cross-compilation, and optional LV2/VST2/Python builds.
